areas.title: The Trireme Euploia
areas.blurb: Captain Nausikles's trireme, carrying you, Kleon and Alethea from Akti across the open sea toward Emporion.
walkthrough: The gangplank comes in and the sail fills the moment you step aboard. Take a lap of the deck first. Two passengers, Phormion the sailor and Lykon the merchant, are happy to battle, and a ladder by the mast drops into the hold, where the rowers sit on their benches.

Alethea stands by the mast with her new Spalunk. She asks for a gentle practice battle. Say yes: losing it costs you nothing, and your team is healed afterward if you do lose. Kleon is bent over the rail, very green, insisting Lakonians never get seasick.

When you're ready, talk to Nausikles at the steering oar in the stern and agree to hold it. The wind dies, the sea goes flat, and the crew has to row. After the lookout shouts, walk forward to the bow. A floating nest is drifting at the ram with snatchers diving on it, and you have to keep them off.

That night the Euploia puts in at Aigina instead of making Emporion. You'll come back on deck the next morning for the last short leg; just watch the mainland come up ahead, and the ship carries you into Emporion's harbor.

key_npcs.label: Nausikles
key_npcs.note: Take the steering oar to start the halcyon calm, the event that moves the story on. After the crossing he runs the ferry: talk to him on deck to make port.

key_npcs.label: Alethea
key_npcs.note: Optional practice battle against her Spalunk (Lv 12). You can't black out; if you lose, your party is healed. One battle only.

statics.condition: The first snatcher at the halcyon nest. You can't run, and losing doesn't send you home.
The second snatcher, straight after the first. Same rules.
Gift. After the nest hatches, one chick hops onto your hat. Answer YES to keep it. It knows Water Gun, Wing Attack, Quick Attack and Mist. Say no and it flies away for good.

tips.text: Say YES to the halcyon chick. Halcyling is a Water and Flying type, and it's the only one you'll be offered on this crossing.
Battle Phormion and Lykon before you take the steering oar. Once the calm starts, the story keeps you busy until the ship reaches Aigina.
The kingfisher's 'halcyon days' are the calm weeks when Aeolus holds the winds so the birds can hatch their eggs on the sea. Nausikles knows the story. He just didn't expect it out here.

spoilers.title: The ship with no lamps
spoilers.text: On the night leg a long dark trireme slides past with no lights and muffled oars. For a moment you can see a sickle on its furled sail. The tide runs the wrong way too, for the third night that month.

spoilers.title: Soon
spoilers.text: A sailor whose cousin is back from Delphoi says the Pythia now answers every question with one word: soon.

areas.title: Aigina Town
areas.blurb: An island harbor halfway to everywhere, where the first coins were struck and the Euploia stops for the night.
walkthrough: You step off the gangplank after dark. Kleon is thrilled to be standing on land, Alethea heads for the mint, and Nausikles tells you the inn is paid for. It stays night here for as long as you're in town.

Before you go to bed, look around. The road north to Aphaia's temple is shut and guarded, so the town is all you can explore tonight. Pheidon the moneyer at the mint will trade, and old Aiakides wants to see an Ergant.

When you're done, go into the inn and tell Endeis you're ready for bed. Kleon and Alethea are waiting by the fire. After the evening's talk your party is healed, and you wake on the Euploia's deck for the last leg to Emporion.

key_npcs.label: Endeis (innkeeper)
key_npcs.note: On the voyage night, answer YES to 'Ready for bed?' to play the night scene, heal your party and sail on. On any later visit she heals your party.

key_npcs.label: Pheidon (moneyer)
key_npcs.note: In-game trade: your Karkipool for his Chelonet, nicknamed STATER. It holds an Oran Berry. One trade only.

key_npcs.label: Aiakides
key_npcs.note: Bring an Ergant anywhere in your party and he gives you a Black Belt. Once only.

key_npcs.label: Nausikles
key_npcs.note: On the voyage night he just sends you to the inn.

key_npcs.label: Gatekeeper
key_npcs.note: Keeps the Aphaia Road gate shut. It opens in Act II, when Nausikles adds Aigina to his ferry.

tips.text: Do your Aigina errands before you talk to Endeis. Once you go to bed the ship sails at first light, and the Euploia's ferry doesn't stop at Aigina again until Act II.
Ergant live on Route 1 and Kronion Hill back on Kalliste. If one is already in your party or Pithos, put it in your party and the Black Belt is yours tonight.
Karkipool turn up in the water around Akti and Route 1. Trade one to Pheidon and you get a Chelonet, which Euphronios the vase-painter in Emporion wants to paint.

Aigina's coins carry a sea turtle, and its people say their ancestors were ants: King Aiakos asked Zeus for as many people as there were ants on an oak, and woke to the Myrmidons. That's why every Ergant in town is called Myrmidon.

spoilers.title: Kleon's prophecy
spoilers.text: By the fire, Kleon admits the Oracle called him 'young and glorious' as a child. Everyone has watched him ever since, and when he loses they look at him 'like I'm already gone'. Alethea vows to find out the real story before it happens to him.

areas.title: Emporion Harbor
areas.blurb: Emporion's busy quay and shipsheds, where every ship in the sea ties up and the rites of the gods are first explained.
walkthrough: Kleon sprints off toward the temple as soon as you land. A man in a winged hat raps his staff on a bollard: Kerykos, Herald of Hermes. He walks you to the herm at the head of the quay and has you pray. That's your first rite. He then gives you three flasks of Olive Oil.

Alethea gives you her spare trowel, Alethea's Trowel, and shows you how to dig in the planter beside the herm. You turn up a painted sherd. She heads off to the Deigma, the merchants' hall, in the city to the north. Make room in your Bag first: the scene won't start until you have space for the oil and the trowel.

Before you head north, look around. Glykera the fishwife fans herself with an odd old drawing, Halitherses the bird-reader gives a daily omen, and the hiring hall at the west end of the shipsheds is signing up dockhands. Nausikles waits on his berth to ferry you back to Akti whenever you like.
Walk north off the quay into Emporion City.

key_npcs.label: Quay herm
key_npcs.note: Kerykos's prayer tutorial happens here. Afterward it's an altar of Hermes: pray, make offerings, check Favor.

key_npcs.label: Planter dig spot
key_npcs.note: Alethea's tutorial dig. A fixed find: a sherd of the Arachne amphora.

key_npcs.label: Shipsheds dig spot
key_npcs.note: A daily dig spot. Needs Alethea's Trowel. Can turn up more Arachne amphora sherds.

key_npcs.label: Altar of Poseidon
key_npcs.note: Isthmian Poseidon's altar at the root of the mole: pray or make offerings.

key_npcs.label: Alethea
key_npcs.note: If you've lost Alethea's Trowel, she waits on the quay and gives you another.

key_npcs.label: Glykera (fishwife)
key_npcs.note: Trade her one Olive Oil for her fan, which is really Daedalus's page I.

key_npcs.label: Halitherses (augur)
key_npcs.note: Meet him once, then come back each day for an omen: a swarm, the weather, a lucky number, a wandering visitor, or Hermes's blessing (YES to accept).

key_npcs.label: Nausikles
key_npcs.note: The ferry. From here it sails to Akti.

key_npcs.label: Crew boss
key_npcs.note: Optional battle. Beat him and he gives you a Rocky Helmet. Once only.

tips.text: Hold on to Kerykos's Olive Oil. One flask buys Daedalus's first page from Glykera, and the great herm in the city takes another. The herms inside the temple use the temple's own free oil.
Visit Halitherses every day. When he says a jar in the Agora barked at a priest, go to the jar with the paw-print by the stoa for a Pithound.
Hermes's blessing from an omen makes Agora prices 20% lower, raises what you get for selling by 20%, and adds 20% to trainer prize money while it lasts.
The pine crown hanging by Poseidon's altar is the prize of the Isthmian Games. Winners there were crowned with pine, not laurel.

spoilers.title: The hiring hall
spoilers.text: The crew boss is Titanborn. His crates are full of shovels and identical bronze helmets, one has a small sickle chalked on it, and he says 'May your thread never be cut.' Half the quay has gone digging for a big man who shouts and pays in silver. After Act I the hall stands empty, and the open ledger reads: ELEUSA. FORTY LAMPS. ALL PAID.

areas.title: Emporion City
areas.blurb: The harbor of the whole wide world: a crowded Agora, a smith's temple, a tavern full of gamblers, and the Temple of Hermes on its terrace.
walkthrough: Start at the Asclepeion on the south side of the city, near the harbor road. Then find the Deigma, the merchants' hall in the south-east. Alethea is inside with Lampis, a lamp-seller who sold some bronze-helmeted customers twenty shovels, a mile of rope and forty lamps. She reads the Archon's notice: the Sacred Way to Eleusa is shut to all but heralds. To go on, you need Kerykos's Herald Laurel.

Next, visit the Hephaisteion, the smith's temple in the north-west of the city. Kedalion's forge went cold during the calm, and only fire from a hearth that has never gone out will light it again. Show him the Charcoal from Hestia's hearth in Akti and the forge roars back to life. He gives you the Bronze Hammer, a relic that breaks rubble. The hoplites at the Isthmus Gate will tell you why you want it.

The Agora fills the middle of town. There's a general stall, an offerings stall, a scroll stall that sells TMs, and Kydon's honey. Pasion the moneychanger buys old coins, and the jars by the stoa sometimes hold a grumpy Pithound. Every house is open: a vase-painter, a hospitable old shipper, a sailor's widow, the runners' barracks and the Dolphin tavern, where they play knucklebones.

When you climb the stair to the Temple of Hermes on the north terrace, Kleon bursts out of the door with the Herald Laurel already tied on. He ran the Herald's Run in sixty-one steps, and he tells you he'll wait at the Isthmus Gate. Head inside for your own laurel.

With the Herald Laurel in hand, go to the Isthmus Gate in the north-west corner. Without it, the hoplites turn you back. Kleon is waiting in the gateway and challenges you to a proper battle. Win or lose, the story carries on, and then the hoplites let you through. North of the gate is Route 4, the Isthmus road. The western Nemea Gate stays shut for now.

key_npcs.label: Healer
key_npcs.note: Heals your party. Emporion's Asclepeion is also where you respawn after a blackout.

key_npcs.label: The Pithos of Emporion
key_npcs.note: Store Pokémon and your stored things.

key_npcs.label: Kedalion (smith)
key_npcs.note: Have Charcoal in your Bag and give him a sliver. He relights the forge and gives you the Bronze Hammer relic, and Hephaestus's Favor rises by 5.

key_npcs.label: General stall
key_npcs.note: Poké Balls and medicine. More stock after the Herald Laurel.

key_npcs.label: Offerings stall
key_npcs.note: Olive Oil, Barley Cake, Wine and Frankincense for the gods' altars.

key_npcs.label: Scroll stall
key_npcs.note: Sells five TMs.

key_npcs.label: Kydon (honey-seller)
key_npcs.note: Sells Honey, the offering Hermes loves most.

key_npcs.label: Pasion (moneychanger)
key_npcs.note: Buys Bronze Obols, Silver Owls and Gold Staters for 20% more than usual.

key_npcs.label: Sykeas (fig-seller)
key_npcs.note: Deal with the snatcher on his awning, by battle or by catching it, and he gives you 3 Figy Berries and a Pretty Feather.

key_npcs.label: Jar with the paw-print
key_npcs.note: On days when Halitherses's omen names it, a Pithound (Lv 16) is hiding inside. Beat it or catch it and it's gone until the omen comes round again.

key_npcs.label: Stoa jar
key_npcs.note: Each check has a 1 in 4 chance of a wild Pithound (Lv 14 to 16).

key_npcs.label: Great herm
key_npcs.note: Anoint it with Olive Oil. Hermes remembers you passed, and his Favor rises by 1.

key_npcs.label: Dig spot by the Hephaisteion
key_npcs.note: A daily dig spot. Needs Alethea's Trowel.

key_npcs.label: Number Nine
key_npcs.note: A wooden statue 'by Daedalus', roped to its plinth. Untie it if you dare.

key_npcs.label: Isthmus Gate
key_npcs.note: Shut until you have the Herald Laurel. Then Kleon's second battle starts here, and afterward the way to Route 4 opens.

key_npcs.label: Thaletas
key_npcs.note: In-game trade: your Onotis for his Narkeray, nicknamed SOCRATES. It holds a Shell Bell.

key_npcs.label: Myrtale (knucklebones champion)
key_npcs.note: Beat her at knucklebones for TM Fling. You can play her again whenever you like.

key_npcs.label: Strepsiades
key_npcs.note: A cautious knucklebones player. Your first win earns 2 Olive Oil.

key_npcs.label: Stratyllis
key_npcs.note: A bold knucklebones player. Your first win earns a Wine.

key_npcs.label: Philoxenos (host)
key_npcs.note: Feeds you, which heals your party, and offers his guest bed to rest. Once you hold the Herald Laurel, tell him the story for a Wine (and again after the Harvest Laurel).

key_npcs.label: Penelopeia
key_npcs.note: Gives you her husband's Sea Incense. Once only.

key_npcs.label: Dromokleia (chief runner)
key_npcs.note: Gives you a Quick Claw on your first visit. After Act I, her runners carry a letter home to your mother.

key_npcs.label: Euphronios (vase-painter)
key_npcs.note: Show him a Harpeck for 2 Super Potions, then a Chelonet for 3 Great Balls, then a Stachyss (from Eleusa) for a Star Piece. One at a time, in that order.

statics.where: On Sykeas's fig-stall awning in the Agora
statics.condition: One battle. Win, lose or catch it, the snatcher is gone afterward, and you can't black out.

statics.where: The jar with the paw-print by the stoa
statics.condition: Only on days when Halitherses's omen sends you here.

statics.where: The stoa jar next to the marked one
statics.condition: A 1 in 4 chance each time you check it. Level 14, 15 or 16.

tips.text: Get the Bronze Hammer before you leave town. The gate hoplites warn that the Titans brought half a hill down on the road past the tombs, and that Kedalion's hammer is the answer.
TM34 at the scroll stall is Shock Wave. Electric moves hit all three of Kerykos's Pokémon super effectively, and Halcyling takes four times the damage.
Trade Pheidon a Karkipool on Aigina and you'll already have the Chelonet Euphronios wants for his second painting. The Harpeck on Sykeas's awning can be caught for the first one.

Kleon's team at the gate is Lophops (Lv 19), Alekrow (Lv 20) and a Lv 21 ace chosen to beat your starter: Dikyon if you picked Nebrel, Thalamare if you picked Kynder, Kladoe if you picked Hipling. Bring something that covers your starter's weakness.
Philoxenos's table heals you for free, and it's closer to the temple than the Asclepeion.
Knucklebones is a best-of-five match. Strepsiades only rethrows his ones and plays it safe; Stratyllis and Myrtale throw boldly.
The man searching the Agora with a lamp for an honest man is borrowed from Diogenes. Kedalion is the smith who carried blind Orion on his shoulders to the sunrise.

spoilers.title: Forty lamps
spoilers.text: The bronze-helmet crew who bought the lamps asked the road to Eleusa and said they'd go round over the goat paths. Alethea works it out: you don't take forty lamps to a field, you take them underground, under Eleusa where the Mysteries are held.

spoilers.title: The hook under the owl
spoilers.text: The Archon's notice closing the Sacred Way has a tiny hook drawn under the owl seal. Alethea brushes it off as a clerk's habit. Remember it.

spoilers.title: Kleon at the gate
spoilers.text: Whether he wins or loses, Kleon admits that winning doesn't feel the way it should. He's heading for the Mysteries at Eleusa because he wants to hear someone say, out loud, that dying isn't the end.

areas.title: Temple of Hermes
areas.blurb: Kerykos's stoa on the city terrace, three terraces of colonnades, turnstiles and herms where you must run the Herald's Run against a step-glass.
walkthrough: Angelos greets you at the door. Kerykos is waiting by the oil jar and the tall step-glass. He explains the rite: carry three sealed scrolls to three herald-herms in the order they're addressed, before the glass runs dry. The glass holds 150 steps on Mortal, 120 on Hero and 100 on Spartan.

Fill your flasks at the jar of temple oil by the door. It's free, and it holds up to three flasks. The junction herms at each fork stare straight ahead until you oil their faces; after that they point the shortest way to the next scroll. Turnstiles only turn one way. A red chevron on the far side shows which way.

Two acolytes, Podarge and Euchidas, stand where you can't slip past them. A third, Philonides, faces the wall and only battles if you talk to him. If the glass runs dry, your scrolls fly back to the door and you start again, but any herm you've oiled stays oiled.

Deliver the third scroll and the bronze gate to the dais swings open. Climb up to Kerykos for the Herald Laurel. Afterward he can send you straight back to the door, and you're free to take the laurel to the Isthmus Gate.

key_npcs.label: Kerykos
key_npcs.note: Starts the Herald's Run. Once all three scrolls are delivered, battle him on the dais. After the laurel he gives TM40 and a Honey, and offers 'the short way down' to the door. Once Hermes's Favor reaches 30, he teaches one of your Pokémon U-turn as Hermes's gift.

key_npcs.label: Angelos (guide)
key_npcs.note: After a failed run he gives a hint about the herms.

key_npcs.label: Jar of temple oil
key_npcs.note: One flask per use, up to three. Free. You lose the flasks when you leave the room.

key_npcs.label: Step-glass
key_npcs.note: During the run, check it for the exact number of steps left.

key_npcs.label: Great altar of Hermes
key_npcs.note: Kerykos's own altar beside the statues on the dais. Offerings left on a god's own temple altar count double.

tips.text: The glass warns you when it's half run and again at 30 steps. If you're lost at the half mark, oil the next junction herm and follow its gaze.
A failed run isn't wasted. Oiled herms stay oiled, so a second attempt with all four junction herms pointing is easy.
Bring Honey. Hermes loves it, and leaving it on his temple altar counts double toward his Favor.
Kerykos comes from the Kerykes, the family of heralds who have called the holy silence at the Eleusinian Mysteries for twenty generations. He ran off to sea instead.

puzzles.title: The Herald's Run
puzzles.hint: Read the plaques: the doorway is the Threshold, the sandal the Road, the purse the Market. Deliver in that order. At every fork, oil the herm and go where it looks, and never take a way down unless a herm points there.
puzzles.solution: Leg 1 (about 11 steps): from Kerykos, follow the red porphyry track east along the porch and through the turnstile at its end, which turns east. Podarge battles you there. The doorway herm (Threshold) stands in the porch's north-east corner; give it the first scroll. The turnstile west of the door only turns east, so don't try it. Leg 2 (about 43 steps): go back west through the turnstile on the gallery row just above, which turns west, and follow the lower gallery all the way to its west end. Take the turnstile stair up, not the passage down; that leads into the archive, a 16-step loop back to the same spot. At the next fork on the middle stoa, take the north lane east. Don't use the south-lane turnstile (wrong way) or the drop (back to the stair). The north lane ends at a turnstile that won't let you through, so drop through the single gap in the colonnade, where Euchidas battles you. Then go east along the south lane and through the east turnstile to the sandal herm (Road). Leg 3 (about 23 steps): climb the east stair north to the upper colonnade and take the north lane under the dais west. The turnstiles beside the stair loop you past Philonides (about 8 extra steps). At the west end, the turnstile turns west into a small pocket, where the purse herm (Market) takes the last scroll. Leg 4 (about 11 steps): the dais gate opens and that turnstile now turns the other way. Walk back east along the north lane and up the steps through the gate to Kerykos. The best possible run is 77 steps.

spoilers.title: Kerykos and Chloe
spoilers.text: Kerykos's cousin is Chloe, who hasn't spoken to him since he ran off to sea. He'll be at Eleusa for the Mysteries, where it's his job to shout 'Silence!'

spoilers.title: The short way
spoilers.text: Kerykos never runs the stoa. He hops the oil jar and takes 'the short way', and he's on the dais before you. Nobody knows where it is.

hierophant.name: Kerykos
hierophant.title: the Herald
hierophant.unlocks: The Isthmus Gate to Route 4 (the Sacred Way's truce lets heralds through), Great Balls, Ice Heals and Super Repels at the Agora's general stall, and +15 Hermes Favor.
strategy: On Hero, Kerykos leads with Lophops (Normal/Flying, Lv 18, Keen Eye), then Halcyling (Water/Flying, Lv 19, Cloud Nine, Oran Berry) and his ace Harpelle (Dark/Flying, Lv 20, Pickpocket, Sitrus Berry). He also carries two Super Potions. Every one of them is part Flying, so Electric and Rock moves are your friends. Shock Wave from the scroll stall never misses and hits Halcyling four times over.

Lophops opens with Feather Dance to cut your Attack, and Harpelle sets up Tailwind to double its team's Speed for a few turns. Special attackers shrug off Feather Dance. Once Tailwind is up, hit hard rather than set up.

Harpelle is the real danger. Once it has eaten its Sitrus Berry, Thief can steal your held item and Pickpocket takes it when you hit Harpelle with a contact move. Taunt shuts down status moves. Finish it fast, or use non-contact moves. Halcyling's Cloud Nine cancels weather, and its Mist blocks your stat drops.

On Mortal his team is three levels lower (15, 16, 17). On Spartan the levels are the same as Hero, but each Pokémon is trained with a nature and EVs, Lophops carries an Oran Berry, he battles with smarter AI, and he has no Super Potions. Spartan's rules also stop you using items in battle.
hierophant.before: Complete the Herald's Run: deliver the three scrolls to the Threshold, Road and Market herms before the step-glass runs dry. Podarge and Euchidas must be beaten on the way; Philonides is optional. All three acolytes count as beaten once you have the laurel.

areas.title: The Aphaia Road
areas.blurb: Aigina's pine-covered interior, climbing from the town gate past pistachio orchards and ant hills to a fork below the island's temple and peak.
walkthrough: This road is shut on the voyage night. Its gate in Aigina Town opens in Act II, once Nausikles adds Aigina to his ferry.

From the gate, the road climbs through the pistachios, west along the lower terrace, north past the ant hills, then east along the upper terrace and through the golden grass to a great herm. There it forks: west to Mount Oros, east up the marble steps to the Temple of Aphaia.

key_npcs.label: Great herm at the fork
key_npcs.note: Anoint it so Hermes remembers you passed.

tips.text: Ergant, Karkipool, Onotis and Chelonet all live along this road. That covers Aiakides's Black Belt, Pheidon's trade and Thaletas's trade in Emporion.

areas.title: Temple of Aphaia
areas.blurb: Aigina's hilltop sanctuary to Aphaia, 'the one who isn't seen', with an altar of Artemis before its dark doorway.
walkthrough: Reached from the east branch of the Aphaia Road's fork in Act II. A path climbs between cypresses and up a second flight of marble steps to the forecourt, where the priestess keeps the temple steps.
East of the altar lie the foundations of an older temple, where the earth has been turned over and something pottery glints. It won't come up by hand.

key_npcs.label: Priestess of Aphaia
key_npcs.note: Keeper of the temple steps.

tips.text: Aphaia is 'the one who isn't seen'. The temple-road gatekeeper says she likes her privacy, and that she's very good at it.

areas.title: Mount Oros
areas.blurb: Aigina's windy peak, crowned by the altar of Zeus where King Aiakos once prayed a drought away.
walkthrough: Take the west branch of the Aphaia Road's fork in Act II. The path climbs through the pines and a band of golden grass to the summit and Zeus's altar. From the top you can see Emporion's masts on the mainland.

tips.text: When all of Greece suffered a drought, the oracle said only Aiakos's prayer would end it. He prayed to Zeus on this mountain, and the rain came.
